meta.subtitle: INGREZZA-led neuroscience biopharma diversifying through CRENESSITY, VYKAT XR and a deep pipeline

advisories: author's published label BUY differs from the composed STRONG BUY

analystSentiment.commentary: We rate Neurocrine Biosciences a BUY with a target range of $150 to $225 against a current price of $140.44. Our probability-weighted fair value is about $184, an expected upside near 31%, with a bear-case downside around 22% and a reward/risk of roughly 1.41x. Q2'26 revenue rose 39.5% to $959.0 million, and the shares trade at 11.7x FY27E and 13.8x next-twelve-months consensus earnings, an undemanding multiple for that growth. Consensus is a Strong Buy with a $208.40 target, 48% above the current price. We hold to a BUY rather than a stronger call because INGREZZA still generated the large majority of product sales, so the durability of that one franchise, and the outcome of the late-stage pipeline, govern the return. Gross margin near 98% and a 6.1% free-cash-flow yield give the business the resources to fund both.

executiveSummary.companyOverview: Neurocrine Biosciences, incorporated in 1992 and based in San Diego, is a neuroscience-focused biopharmaceutical company. Its approved products are INGREZZA (valbenazine) for tardive dyskinesia and chorea associated with Huntington's disease, CRENESSITY (crinecerfont) for congenital adrenal hyperplasia, and VYKAT XR for hyperphagia in Prader-Willi syndrome, alongside Orilissa and Oriahnn in endometriosis and uterine fibroids through a collaboration with AbbVie. FY25 revenue was $2.9 billion, up 21.4%, at a gross margin near 98% typical of a branded-pharmaceutical model. The company runs a diversified mid- to late-stage pipeline across psychiatry, endocrinology and neurology, and is expanding into biologics, peptides and gene therapy. It reports as a single segment.

thesis.label: BUY
thesis.body: The thesis is a fast-growing, cash-generative franchise trading at a modest forward multiple. Q2'26 revenue of $959.0 million rose 39.5% year over year, and the shares trade at 11.7x FY27E and 13.8x next-twelve-months consensus earnings. That valuation looks low for a business compounding revenue in the 20%-to-40% range, which is the source of the upside. The offset is concentration: results still lean heavily on INGREZZA, and the forward earnings power partly depends on late-stage trial outcomes that are inherently binary. Our BUY reflects an expected upside near 31% against a bear-case downside near 22%, a reward/risk of about 1.41x; we would rate it higher were the revenue base less concentrated in a single product.

catalysts: CRENESSITY ramp: Q2'26 net product sales reached $183.5 million, up from $53.2 million a year earlier, as the CAH launch scales.
VYKAT XR added the Prader-Willi franchise through the approximately $2.9 billion all-cash acquisition of Soleno in May 2026, contributing $54.3 million of Q2'26 net sales.
Late-stage pipeline readouts, including Phase 3 programs for osavampator in major depressive disorder and direclidine in schizophrenia, plus an early obesity program.
INGREZZA qualified for the Medicare small-biotech exception, exempting it from price-negotiation selection until 2027 with initial price applicability in 2029, which defers the pricing risk.
Consensus is a Strong Buy at a $208.40 target, about 48% above the current price, with 24 of 28 analysts rating the shares Buy.
risks: Product concentration: INGREZZA still drives the large majority of net product sales, so a competitive or pricing setback there would dominate results.
Drug pricing: the Inflation Reduction Act and other reforms could pressure INGREZZA once its Medicare exemption lapses.
Pipeline risk: the late-stage programs are binary, and a Phase 3 failure would remove a pillar of the growth case.
Integration risk: the company may not realize the anticipated benefits of the Soleno acquisition or fully integrate VYKAT XR.
Operational dependence: the company has no manufacturing capability and relies on a limited number of third-party suppliers.

income.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.incomeCommentary: Q2'26 revenue was $959.0 million, up 39.5% year over year, and first-half net product sales rose 41.7% to $1.77 billion, an increase of $519.6 million. Operating income was $151.5 million, a 15.8% operating margin, held down by Soleno acquisition-related expenses that included $23.1 million in payroll and benefits, of which $18.1 million was accelerated stock-based compensation. Research and development was $326.7 million in the quarter, 34.1% of revenue, reflecting the Phase 3 osavampator and direclidine programs and an expanding early-stage portfolio. FY25 revenue was $2.9 billion, up 21.4%, with net income of $478.6 million and diluted EPS of $4.67. Consensus estimates are set on an adjusted basis that excludes items such as acquired in-process research, intangible amortization and acquisition costs; on that basis they call for EPS of $10.20 in FY26E and $11.97 in FY27E, which is why the forward multiples sit well below the trailing GAAP P/E. We treat the forward multiples as adjusted-basis figures.

balance.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.balanceCommentary: The balance sheet remains sound after the Soleno deal. FY25 cash and short-term investments were about $0.7 billion and total equity was $3.3 billion, up from $1.4 billion in FY21, and the balance sheet shows no term debt. In May 2026 the company entered a $1.0 billion senior secured revolving credit facility, drew and then repaid $600.0 million, and had the full $1.0 billion of capacity available as of June 30, 2026. The current ratio was 3.39 at FY25, though the trailing figure of 1.87 reflects the cash deployed and liabilities assumed in funding the Soleno acquisition. The available revolver leaves the company financing flexibility for further business development.

cashflow.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.cashflowCommentary: Cash generation is strong for a company at this growth rate. FY25 operating cash flow was about $0.8 billion against minimal capital expenditure of $34 million, producing free cash flow of $748.7 million at a 26.2% margin and a 6.1% free-cash-flow yield. The company pays no dividend and returns cash through buybacks: FY25 share repurchases were $167.7 million, part of a $500.0 million repurchase program the Board authorized in 2025. Free cash flow of this scale funds both the pipeline and opportunistic business development such as the Soleno acquisition without straining the balance sheet.

multiples.note: Peer multiples pending a peer data source.

valuation.multiplesCommentary: The shares trade at 20.6x trailing GAAP earnings and 4.2x sales, falling to 13.8x next-twelve-months and 11.7x FY27E on adjusted consensus earnings. The gap between the trailing and forward multiples is wide because the forward estimates are struck on an adjusted basis and because earnings are growing quickly. No peer multiple set was available in this pack, so we value the company on its own forward earnings, its free-cash-flow yield and the scale of its addressable markets. The scenarios hinge on INGREZZA's durability, the CRENESSITY and VYKAT XR ramps, and the read-through from the late-stage pipeline.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: INGREZZA holds share, CRENESSITY and VYKAT XR scale, and one or more late-stage programs succeed, letting the multiple re-rate toward the Strong Buy consensus. Implied price near $235, above the median $214.00 target and toward the $253.00 top of the analyst range.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: The commercial portfolio keeps compounding at a decelerating rate, the adjusted FY27E EPS of $11.97 is broadly met, and the forward multiple expands modestly from today's low level. Implied price about $185, below the $208.40 consensus target.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: INGREZZA faces new competition or pricing pressure, a key Phase 3 program disappoints, or Soleno integration falls short, and the shares de-rate below their 52-week low. Implied price near $110, roughly 22% below the current $140.44 and under the $122.14 low of the range.

valuation.scenarioCommentary: Weighting the Bull at 30%, the Base at 48% and the Bear at 22% gives a fair value of about $184, an expected upside near 31% and a bear-case downside of roughly 22%, for a reward/risk of about 1.41x. That risk/reward would support a stronger rating on the numbers alone; we hold to BUY because the Bear is a genuine, product-specific scenario rather than a formality. INGREZZA is the principal swing factor, and the multiple already reflects the market's discount for that concentration, which is also why the downside is contained relative to a richer-multiple name.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: Neurocrine reports as a single segment. Q2'26 net product sales of $954.3 million comprised INGREZZA at $716.5 million, CRENESSITY at $183.5 million, VYKAT XR at $54.3 million and other products at $4.4 million, with an additional $4.7 million of collaboration revenue from royalties on AbbVie and Tanabe sales. The mix is diversifying as CRENESSITY and the newly acquired VYKAT XR scale, but INGREZZA remains the dominant contributor. Each product addresses a defined patient population: the company estimates tardive dyskinesia affects about 800,000 people in the U.S., congenital adrenal hyperplasia at least 20,000, and hyperphagia in Prader-Willi syndrome about 10,000.

moatFactors.name: INGREZZA franchise and VMAT2 leadership
moatFactors.body: INGREZZA was the first FDA-approved drug for tardive dyskinesia in 2017 and anchors the company's position in VMAT2 biology, supported by a commercial infrastructure and sales force built and expanded since launch.

moatFactors.name: First-in-class rare-disease positions
moatFactors.body: CRENESSITY is a first-in-class treatment for congenital adrenal hyperplasia and VYKAT XR the first and only approved treatment for hyperphagia in Prader-Willi syndrome, both addressing under-served conditions with limited direct competition today.

moatFactors.name: Pipeline and R&D depth
moatFactors.body: A diversified mid- to late-stage pipeline across psychiatry, endocrinology and neurology, backed by R&D of $326.7 million in Q2'26, extends the franchise beyond the current products, though each program carries clinical and regulatory risk.

moatFactors.name: Concentration and external dependence
moatFactors.body: The moat is narrowed by reliance on INGREZZA for most sales, by patent and competitive exposure, and by the absence of in-house manufacturing, which leaves the company dependent on a limited number of third-party suppliers.

businessMoat.durability: Durability is anchored by INGREZZA's established position and by the Medicare small-biotech exception that defers price-negotiation exposure until 2027, with initial price applicability in 2029. The first-in-class CRENESSITY and VYKAT XR positions and the breadth of the pipeline extend the runway. The offsetting risk is that a single-product concentration meets eventual patent expiry, competition and drug-pricing reform, so the durability of the whole depends on the newer products and the pipeline maturing before INGREZZA's advantages erode.

points: CRENESSITY continues to scale following its December 2024 CAH launch, and expert data on pediatric growth and cardiometabolic outcomes support broader adoption.
VYKAT XR adds a Prader-Willi franchise, and management is expanding the INGREZZA and CRENESSITY sales teams to press commercial momentum.
Late-stage programs for osavampator in major depressive disorder and direclidine in schizophrenia, plus a Phase 2 M1/M4 agonist, target large psychiatric markets.
An early obesity program, NBIP-2118, and a move into biologics, peptides and gene therapy broaden the modality base beyond small molecules.
Expanded formulary access covers approximately 70% of tardive dyskinesia and Huntington's disease Medicare beneficiaries, supporting INGREZZA volume growth.

management.leadership: Per the 2026 proxy, Kyle W. Gano, Ph.D., is Chief Executive Officer, with Matthew C. Abernethy as Chief Financial Officer, Eric Benevich as Chief Commercial Officer, Sanjay Keswani, M.D., as Chief Medical Officer, and Jude Onyia, Ph.D., as Chief Scientific Officer; Kevin Gorman, Ph.D., is the former CEO and remains a director. During 2026 the company promoted Samir Siddhanti to Chief Business Officer and Andrew Ratz, Ph.D., to Chief Technical Operations Officer, the latter to lead the expansion into biologics and device-based therapies. The team has commercialized three products since INGREZZA's 2017 launch.
management.capitalAllocation: The company pays no dividend and allocates capital to R&D, buybacks and business development. It repurchased $167.7 million of stock in FY25 under a $500.0 million program authorized by the Board in 2025, which followed a $300.0 million program completed in February 2025. The main capital action was the roughly $2.9 billion all-cash acquisition of Soleno in May 2026, funded from cash and the new revolving facility. The company also sold Neurocrine Group Limited to Immedica for $63.2 million in January 2026, recognizing a $28.6 million pre-tax gain.
management.governance: Per the 2026 proxy, all directors are independent under Nasdaq standards except current CEO Kyle Gano and former CEO Kevin Gorman. The Board is classified into three classes with staggered terms, which the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee reviews annually and considers appropriate given the multi-year development cycles of the company's programs. A staggered board can slow a change of control. An overboarding policy limits directors to a maximum of five public-company boards, and the proxy states all directors comply.
management.insiderOwnership: Insider ownership is modest and institutions hold the swing votes. Per the 2026 proxy, 100,581,991 shares were outstanding as of March 31, 2026, and all executive officers and directors as a group, 20 persons, held 4,768,380 shares, or 4.6%. The larger individual holders are former CEO Kevin C. Gorman with 1,572,104 shares, or 1.5%, and current CEO Kyle W. Gano with 635,601. Institutional positions are far larger: BlackRock at 12.0% (12,052,271 shares), Vanguard at 10.1%, Dodge & Cox at 5.5% and JPMorgan Chase at 5.2%. The BlackRock and Vanguard figures rest on Schedule 13G/A filings reporting ownership in early 2025, so both predate this filing and may have changed. The low aggregate insider stake against double-digit institutional holders means outside institutions, not management, carry the register.

idiosyncratic: Product concentration: INGREZZA generates the large majority of Q2'26 net product sales, as the segment breakdown shows, so any competitive entry, safety signal or reimbursement change affecting it would have an outsized impact.
Drug-pricing reform: the 10-Q flags the Inflation Reduction Act and other measures as risks; INGREZZA's Medicare exemption defers but does not eliminate future price-negotiation exposure.
Clinical and regulatory risk: late-stage programs such as osavampator and direclidine are subject to trial failure or delay, which would remove a growth pillar the valuation partly assumes.
Acquisition integration: the company may fail to integrate Soleno or realize the anticipated benefits of adding VYKAT XR to its rare-disease portfolio.
Supply and manufacturing dependence: with no in-house manufacturing, disruption at a limited number of third-party suppliers could impair commercialization and trials.
risks.systemic: The main systemic exposure is U.S. healthcare and drug-pricing policy. The Inflation Reduction Act's Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program, changes to formulary access, and payor reimbursement decisions can all compress branded-pharmaceutical revenue regardless of a product's clinical merit. The company also depends on continued access to capital markets to fund research and business development, and on a regulatory approval process whose standards and timelines can shift. A broad tightening of any of these would weigh on the sector and on the multiple investors are willing to pay for future pipeline value.

body: We rate Neurocrine Biosciences a BUY with a $150 to $225 target range around a probability-weighted fair value of about $184, an expected upside near 31% and a reward/risk of roughly 1.41x. The company is growing quickly and cheaply valued on forward earnings: Q2'26 revenue rose 39.5% to $959.0 million, CRENESSITY and VYKAT XR are diversifying the base, and a gross margin near 98% with a 6.1% free-cash-flow yield funds both the pipeline and acquisitions like Soleno.

The reason we do not go higher, despite risk/reward that would support it, is concentration and binary risk. INGREZZA still drives the large majority of sales, the late-stage pipeline outcomes are uncertain, and drug-pricing reform is a standing threat even with INGREZZA's Medicare exemption to 2027. The Bear, about 22% below the current price and below the 52-week low, is the case where INGREZZA stumbles or a Phase 3 program fails. We would accumulate in the lower half of our range and size the position for the single-product risk.
